alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain with metabolic deterioration
alerts.message: Guidelines state clinicians should discuss the possibility of weight gain when starting ART, as obesity is an increasing problem particularly among women, and proactive diet and exercise advice should be given to all patients starting or switching ART. Patient gained 17kg (65→82kg) and BMI rose from 25.6 to 32.4 within 18 months of switching from EFV to DTG. Acanthosis nigricans indicates insulin resistance. Fasting glucose worsened from 92 to 118 mg/dL (impaired fasting glucose), HbA1c 6.1% is pre-diabetic. Lipid profile is atherogenic: LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212. BP rose from 118/74 to 138/88. Family history of Type 2 Diabetes compounds this risk. DTG is strongly associated with greater weight gain than EFV; EFV discontinuation may have unmasked weight gain previously suppressed by EFV. Virologic suppression is excellent (VL <50, CD4 612).

evidence.recommended_action: Provide proactive diet and exercise counselling. Consider glucose monitoring every 3 months per DTG transition guidance. Evaluate for metformin or GLP-1 agonist eligibility. Consider ART switch if metabolic parameters continue worsening despite lifestyle intervention.

alerts.title: No assessment or plan documented for metabolic abnormalities
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after transition to DTG. This patient transitioned 18 months ago and today's labs show impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL), pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%), and dyslipidaemia, yet the clinician's assessment and plan field is blank with no orders documented. No follow-up glucose monitoring, lipid management, or weight management plan has been recorded despite multiple clinically significant metabolic abnormalities that warrant intervention. The patient also reports fatigue, which could relate to insulin resistance, developing diabetes, or other causes.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and management plan addressing weight gain, pre-diabetes, dyslipidaemia, and hypertension. Schedule glucose monitoring at least every 3 months. Consider dietary counselling, lipid follow-up, and evaluation of fatigue.

alerts.title: Pre-diabetes and borderline hypertension require monitoring
alerts.message: Patient has pre-diabetes (HbA1c 6.1%, fasting glucose 118 mg/dL) with acanthosis nigricans and family history of Type 2 Diabetes, placing her at high risk of progression to overt diabetes. BP of 138/88 mmHg represents elevated blood pressure bordering on hypertension, up from a baseline of 118/74. Guidelines note weight gain as an increasing problem in HIV care. The combination of obesity (BMI 32.4), pre-diabetes, dyslipidaemia (LDL 148, triglycerides 212, HDL 38), and rising BP constitutes a compounding cardiometabolic risk profile. Each abnormality alone may not trigger immediate intervention, but together they significantly increase cardiovascular and diabetes risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule repeat fasting glucose and HbA1c in 3 months. Monitor BP at each visit. Consider formal oral glucose tolerance test. Evaluate need for statin therapy per cardiovascular risk assessment.
